Foreign-key relationships link enrollments.account_id to accounts.id and enrollments.offering_id to offerings.id.
Seeded offerings identify courses, semesters, sections, and capacities.
Semester-filtered course catalog with capacities and registration actions.
The student starts with an empty Fall 2026 schedule.
Before first registration: enrollments contains zero rows.
After first registration and before adding another class: Alex (account_id 1) is enrolled in offering 1.
The schedule displays the first registered class.
After adding a class and before deletion: account_id 1 has offering_id 1 and 2.
Two registered classes total six credits; Add more courses returns to the same semester.
A separate confirmation page identifies the exact class and explains the seat release.
After confirmed deletion: offering 1 is removed while offering 2 remains for the same student.
The refreshed schedule contains only Database Systems after removal.
Summer 2027 has no seeded offerings and displays the empty-term message.
The waiting-list page identifies the course, semester, and queue position.
Cancellation creates a reserved-seat notice for Alex with an acceptance link and expiration.
The offer page supports explicit acceptance or decline.
Before acceptance: one pending reservation retains its recipient and waiting-list entry.
After acceptance: status is accepted and waiting_id is cleared; the recipient remains recorded.
Profile editing retains the existing account identity while allowing contact updates.
